clauses.current_legal_basis: The order's own held text (16 FR 11907) has no end, and the bounded searches found no later instrument. The U.S. Code (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09) prints the order as an editorial note under 18 U.S.C. 3496 with no ending statement, and the held text of 18 U.S.C. 3496 still authorizes the President to prescribe the commission and witness-fee regulations. 22 CFR 92.65 (eCFR as of 2026-10-14) lists E.O. 10307 in its authority line. Checked through 2026-10-14.
clauses.reason: The sole paragraph delegates to the Secretary of State (1) the authority vested in the President by 18 U.S.C. 3496 to prescribe regulations on executing and returning consular commissions and schedules of fees for witnesses, foreign counsel and interpreters, and (2) the authority under 18 U.S.C. 3492(c) to prescribe regulations making sections 3492-3496 applicable to diplomatic officers; it also revokes Executive Order 8298 of December 4, 1939. The delegation states no duration, condition or event that ends it. The held text of 18 U.S.C. 3496 still reads that the President is authorized to prescribe those regulations, the U.S. Code still prints this order under that section, and the current Department of State regulation 22 CFR 92.65 cites E.O. 10307 as authority, so the delegation is operative on 2026-10-14. The revocation of Executive Order 8298 was complete on issuance and is recorded as a surviving consequence, not as a continuing command.

research_rationale:
Read the whole order (16 FR 11907, signed 1951-11-23): one paragraph delegating to the Secretary of State the President's authority under 18 U.S.C. 3496 and 3492(c) to prescribe consular-commission regulations and witness-fee schedules and to apply sections 3492-3496 to diplomatic officers, and revoking Executive Order 8298 of December 4, 1939. The order has no own-terms end. The three bounded searches were read against their coverage notes: current-law:usc (release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09) hits the U.S. Code note printing the order under 18 U.S.C. 3496 with no ending statement; current-law:ecfr (as of 2026-10-14) hits 22 CFR 92.65 (authority line lists E.O. 10307) and 22 CFR 92.70; later-events:ofr_catalog has no hit. The held text of 18 U.S.C. 3496 still authorizes the President to prescribe those regulations. Limitation disclosed: the packet does not hold the text of 3 U.S.C. 301 (the general delegation statute cited in the order as the act of August 8, 1950); the delegated power itself rests on 18 U.S.C. 3496, which is held.

savings.reason: The order has no saving clause. The only surviving consequence is that Executive Order 8298 stays revoked; no held source restores it. No pending-matter residue was found by the three bounded searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Office of the Federal Register disposition notes), so the state is none after bounded search.
